text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me if these frightened awakenings happen right after you fall asleep or later in the night, and do you remember a nightmare when you wake up?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any specific memories of scary dreams during these episodes, and do you ever sit up in bed or get out of bed while seemingly asleep? I also need to know if you have been under significant stress at school or home recently.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you remember the bad dreams and can be consoled, this sounds like nightmares rather than night terrors, but I need to rule out other causes. Do you have any other symptoms like snoring, pauses in breathing during sleep, or daytime hyperactivity? REQUEST TEST: Polysomnography
